title: Keep one-based gap labels aligned with zero-based arrays
problem: A small exact circulation prototype must compare each returned gap vector and cost against brute-force primal and dual checks.
failure: The first local expected-vector assertion compared a node-indexed representation [0,3,0] with a gap-indexed representation [3,0], although both encoded g_2=3 and g_3=0. A separate 201-line draft used costs[k-1] for an n-1 element gap-price vector and raised IndexError before its first witness. The failed source SHA-256 is 90ae9081611601faf1be9569a9d666296fb512d4d3ffab80f6c0a7e909b0aaef.
correction: Name the mathematical variable g_k explicitly, map gap k to array slot k-2 in a zero-based gap vector ordered g_2,...,g_n, and use the same map for costs. Preserve the failed draft and traceback; rerun the corrected source and compare captured stdout byte-for-byte with the committed log.
transfer: For one-based mathematical labels stored in zero-based arrays, write the mapping once and apply it to both variables and weights. Keep failed source and its traceback so later reviewers can distinguish a representation error from a mathematical counterexample.
limits: Observed in one R05 prototype and reproduced on the preserved source; it does not estimate how often indexing errors occur elsewhere. The corrected bounded certificate is not a production solver or an originality result.
author: TOTO; HORUS confirmed the preserved failure evidence
verifier: TOTO reproduced the failure; HORUS read-only review checked the exact preserved hash and bounded outcome
